purpose: Document the prevalence of the Russian official/media narrative that Russia is effectively fighting NATO, the United States, or the collective West through Ukraine, and distinguish that narrative from separately verifiable facts about foreign volunteers serving in Ukrainian formations.
epistemic_firewall: Frequency of repetition is evidence of narrative prevalence, not proof the narrative is factually correct.

Foreign volunteers from many countries serving in Ukrainian units are real and officially acknowledged by Ukraine; this does not by itself establish that NATO member states are belligerents or that their regular armies are secretly fighting as a bloc.
Opinion polling measures reported beliefs under Russian political and media conditions; it should not be converted into a claim about literally every Russian citizen.
Official statements, state media repetition, and mass-attitude polling are stored as separate evidence layers.

official_russian_state_layer.speaker: Sergey Kiriyenko
official_russian_state_layer.role: First Deputy Chief of Staff of the Presidential Administration of Russia
official_russian_state_layer.claim_summary: NATO is fighting Russia on Ukrainian territory and with Ukrainian hands.

official_russian_state_layer.speaker: Sergey Shoigu
official_russian_state_layer.role: Russian Defence Minister at the time
official_russian_state_layer.claim_summary: Russia is fighting not so much Ukraine as the collective West and NATO.

official_russian_state_layer.speaker: Anatoly Antonov
official_russian_state_layer.role: Russian Ambassador to the United States at the time
official_russian_state_layer.claim_summary: The United States is pursuing a war of attrition against Russia through Ukrainians.

official_russian_state_layer.speaker: Vladimir Putin
official_russian_state_layer.claim_summary: Russia has been fighting not the Ukrainian Armed Forces or Ukraine but practically all NATO countries; he also stated that many countries and NATO instructors participate in the conflict.

recurrent_elements: US and other foreign nationals fighting on Ukraine's side
foreign fighters portrayed as representatives of NATO states
Ukraine presented as an instrument of Western confrontation with Russia

mass_attitude_layer.finding: 60 percent of respondents considered the United States and NATO countries the initiators of escalation in eastern Ukraine before the full-scale invasion.
57 percent assigned responsibility for deaths and destruction in Ukraine to the United States and NATO countries; 7 percent assigned responsibility to Russia.
56 percent assigned responsibility for deaths and destruction in Ukraine to the United States and NATO; 60 percent considered a direct Russia-NATO armed conflict possible.
65 percent assigned responsibility for deaths and destruction in Ukraine to the United States and NATO. Among respondents who trusted television as an information source, the share was 74 percent.
92 percent of respondents said contemporary Russia has enemies, the highest value since 1994; the United States, European Union, Ukraine and United Kingdom were named among the principal enemies.

54 percent considered it possible that the conflict in Ukraine could develop into an armed conflict between Russia and NATO countries; negative attitudes toward the United States, EU and NATO predominated in contemporaneous polling.

foreign_fighter_fact_control.finding: Ukraine officially acknowledges foreign volunteers from more than 50 countries in its International Legion structures; Ukrainian Defence Intelligence stated in 2024 that volunteers from 55 countries were fighting in the DIU International Legion.
foreign_fighter_fact_control.interpretation: The existence of foreign volunteers is a real underlying fact repeatedly used in Russian messaging. It does not by itself prove the stronger proposition that NATO as an alliance or the US military is directly waging the war as a belligerent through Ukraine.

assessment.best_defensible_summary: The framing that the conflict is fundamentally a confrontation with the United States, NATO or the collective West is not a fringe Russian narrative. It has been repeated by senior state officials and major state/pro-government media for years, while representative polling repeatedly finds majority-level attribution of responsibility to the United States and NATO.

relevance_to_tspu_external_us_impact: If exported censorship/DPI systems are activated in foreign information environments, the Russian domestic case provides a concrete warning model: restricting access to alternative information channels can coexist with sustained repetition of an external-enemy narrative. Establishing causality between filtering and attitude change requires longitudinal measurements and controls rather than rhetoric counts alone.
